chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from one of his companions, from Mansur ibn Hazam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married a Zimmiyyah (non-Muslim woman under treaty) over a Muslim woman, and did not ask her permission. He said: 'And they are separated.' I said: 'So is there discipline upon him?' He said: 'Yes, twelve lashes, and half of eighty being the Hadd of the adulterer, and he is Saqir (belittled/disgraced).' I said: 'So if the free Muslim woman were to be pleased with his deed after what he had done?' He said: 'He is not whipped, nor are they separated between them; they remain upon the first marriage.'

key_terms.حَدُّ الزَّانِي: The fixed legal punishment for adultery
key_terms.ذِمِّيَّةٌ: A non-Muslim woman under the protection of the Islamic state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a non-Muslim woman over a Muslim woman without her permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific penalty of twelve and a half lashes for a man who marries a Zimmiyyah without his Muslim wife's consent, categorizing it as a discretionary punishment (Ta'ir) rather than a fixed Hadd. The ruling highlights the principle of 'Saghr' (disgrace) in marital discretion, yet allows for the preservation of the marriage if the wife grants her consent, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the wife's rights within the polygamous structure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from one of his companions, from Mansour Bin Hazam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about a man who married a Zimmi woman (woman under the responsibility of the Islamic government) over a Muslim woman, (as a second wife) and did not have her instructions (permission). Heasws said: ‘And there would be separation between the two of them’. So I said, ‘So is there disciplining upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twelve lashes, and half of eighty being a Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled’. I said, ‘So if the free Muslim woman were to be happy with his deed after what he had done?’ Heasws said: ‘He would not be whipped, nor would there be separation between the two. They would both remain upon the first marriage’.
